chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Sa'id al-Makari, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah: 'By what will the Imam be recognized?' He said: 'By calmness and gravity.' I said: 'And by what?' He said: 'You will know him by the halal and the haram, and by the need of people to him, and he will not need anyone, and the weapon of the Messenger of Allah will be with him.' I said: 'Will he be only a guardian, the son of a guardian?' He said: 'He will be only a guardian and the son of a guardian.'

key_terms.الْحَلَالِ وَالْحَرَامِ: The permissible and the forbidden (executing divine law)
key_terms.سِلَاحُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The weapon of the Messenger of Allah (symbol of authority and victory)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and characteristics used to recognize the Imam al-Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the physical and spiritual markers of the Imam, particularly al-Mahdi, by linking his inner tranquility (sakinah) with his independent authority in jurisprudence and his self-sufficiency from worldly needs. The mention of 'the Prophet's weapon' is interpreted by Shia scholars as a symbol of divine authority and readiness for leadership, while the lineage confirmation reinforces the concept of *Nass* (designation) within the Ahl al-Bayt. These traits collectively establish his legitimacy as the final Wasi of the Prophet Muhammad.
